messages.content: Write `nQueens(n)` — count solutions to n-queens using backtracking. Test `n=4`.

<think>
n-Queens backtracking: place one queen per row, track which columns and diagonals are used.
For each row, try each column - skip if column or either diagonal is occupied.
When all n rows placed, increment count.
Diagonals identified by (row-col) and (row+col).
</think>
```falcon
func nQueens(n) = {
  local count = 0
  local cols = []
  local diag1 = []
  local diag2 = []
  func bt(row) = {
    if row > n then {
      count = count + 1
    } else {
      for (c: 1 .. n) {
        if cols.contains(c) == false and diag1.contains(row - c) == false and diag2.contains(row + c) == false then {
          cols.append(c)
          diag1.append(row - c)
          diag2.append(row + c)
          bt(row + 1)
          cols.removeAt(cols.length())
          diag1.removeAt(diag1.length())
          diag2.removeAt(diag2.length())
        }
      }
    }
  }
  bt(1)
  count
}
```

```falcon
func jumpGame(list) = {
```

Longest palindromic substring length: expand around center approach.
For each character (and between characters), expand while chars match.
Track max length found.
</think>
```falcon
func longestPalindrome(s) = {
  local n = s.length()
  local maxLen = 1
  func expand(l, r) = {
    local left = l
    local right = r
    while left >= 1 and right <= n and s.segment(left, left) === s.segment(right, right) do {
      local len = right - left + 1
      if len > maxLen then maxLen = len
      left = left - 1
      right = right + 1
```

```falcon
func gameOfLife(grid) = {
  local rows = grid.length()
  local cols = grid[1].length()
  local next = []
  for (r: 1 .. rows) {
    local row = []
    for (c: 1 .. cols) {
      local live = 0
      for (dr: -1 .. 1) {
        for (dc: -1 .. 1) {
          if dr == 0 and dc == 0 then {} else {
            local nr = r + dr
            local nc = c + dc

      local nxt = if cur == 1 then (if live == 2 or live == 3 then 1 else 0) else (if live == 3 then 1 else 0)
      row.append(nxt)
    }
    next.append(row)
  }
  next
}
```

Partition count using pentagonal number theorem: p(n) = sum of (-1)^(k+1) * p(n - k*(3k-1)/2)
for k = 1,-1,2,-2,... while pentagonal number <= n.

```falcon
func partitionCount(n) = {
  local p = [1]

    p.append(0)
```

```falcon
func bayesUpdate(prior, observations, pHead) = {
  local posterior = {}
  for (pair: prior.toPairs()) {
    posterior[pair[1]] = pair[2]

    local likelihood_H = if obs === "H" then pHead else 1 - pHead
```
